event.text: Has she had ear discharge, itching inside the ear, or recent water exposure (swimming or bathing)?
event.why: Discharge or itching suggests external otitis; water exposure is a key trigger. These would change the clinical picture from isolated pain.

event.text: Home care and watching are reasonable now: right ear pain since last night, no fever reported, she ate breakfast and went to school. Most short-lived ear pain in a child this age settles; an over-the-counter children's pain reliever per its label can help comfort. If the pain persists beyond about 2-3 days, worsens, or she develops fever, ear discharge, or swelling, redness or tenderness behind the ear or an ear that sticks out, arrange in-person assessment that day (urgent care if your usual clinic is unavailable). If she becomes stiff-necked, abnormally drowsy or confused, or develops a purple rash, go to an emergency department immediately.
